dct_description_sm: Located in the Svalbartunga valley (istilfjrur shelf, northeast of Iceland), the Svalbar farm was established in the 10th century and is still active. During the last 1000 years, several secondary farms were also established in the valley. Most of these farms were abandoned at various times but the reasons remain unclear. Since the 1990s, archaeological researches are underway in this valley but limited paleo-environmental researches have been done. The aim of this project is the reconstitution of paleo-environmental conditions of Svalbartunga valley in response to recent climate change and human impact. Specific objectives are 1) to date the peatlands establishment in Svalbartunga valley and to understand their temporal evolution, 2) to document the lake evolution in the vicinity of a secondary farm, 3) to estimate the impacts of known climatic periods on the evolution of peatlands and lakes (Little Ice Age and Medieval Climate Optimum) and 4) to identify anthropogenic signatures preserved in lacustrine sediments. The following hypothesis is to be tested: Due to extreme climate conditions, the wetlands located on the Northeast shore of the island will be more affected by climate and anthropogenic activities compared to other coastal regions of Iceland.

dct_title_s: Wetland dynamics within the Northeast region of Iceland in response to recent climate change and human impact
